the Langmuir model is the best model to be applied in most cases of adsorption systems.
the Langmuir model is the most used model in the literature and the Freundlich model is the most suitable model for describing adsorption isotherns.
the Langmuir, Sips, Toth, Redlich-Peterson, Dubinin-Radushkevich, Freundlich, and Temkin isotherm models are the best isotherm models for the prediction of equilibrium adsorption data.

the use of adsorption isothems for the determination of adsorption capacity of adsorbents and adsorption kinetics, and also the determination of the equilibrium adsorption data.
the selection of optimum isotherm models for adsorption equilibrium data analysis.
the adsorption equilibrium modelling of different systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Freundlich isotherm model is the best model for describing the adsorption of the adsorbate onto the adsorbent in liquid phase, whereas Langmuir isotherm model can be considered as the best isotherm model in gas phase adsorption systems.

the Langmuir model is the most widely used and applied isotherm model in the adsorption studies, followed by the Freundlich, Sips, Redlich–Peterson, and Temkin isotherm models, respectively, while the Toth, Langmuir–Freundlich, Jovanovic, and Sips isotherm models are the least applied isotherm models.
the Freundlich and Langmuir isotherm equations are the most widely used isotherm equations.
